edges.prerequisite: Reliable Transfer over a Perfectly Reliable Channel (rdt1.0)
edges.dependent: Reliable Transfer over a Channel with Bit Errors (rdt2.x)
edges.rationale: rdt2.x builds directly on the rdt1.0 baseline by incrementally adding checksums, ACKs/NAKs, retransmissions, and sequence numbers to the same sender/receiver FSM framework.

edges.prerequisite: Reliable Transfer over a Channel with Bit Errors (rdt2.x)
edges.dependent: Reliable Transfer over a Lossy Channel (rdt3.0)
edges.rationale: rdt3.0 extends rdt2.2 by adding a countdown timer to handle lost packets; its duplicate-detection relies on the sequence-number machinery introduced in rdt2.x.

edges.prerequisite: Reliable Transfer over a Lossy Channel (rdt3.0)
edges.rationale: The utilization analysis quantifies the bandwidth waste of the completed stop-and-wait protocol (rdt3.0), using its sender behavior and RTT/L/R timing model.
The poor utilization derived here is the explicit motivation for pipelined operation, which GBN implements via its sliding window of N outstanding packets.
SR is likewise a pipelined protocol whose design is motivated by the stop-and-wait utilization problem quantified in this analysis.

SR is best understood as a refinement of GBN's sliding-window approach: its individual ACKs, receiver buffering, and window-size constraint relative to the sequence-number space are defined in contrast to GBN's cumulative ACKs and out-of-order discarding.
